subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion/path-hygiene contract now, and should that contract cover builtin indexing only or builtin plus QMD, status diagnostics, and index identity together?
rationale: The remaining work adds a public compatibility-sensitive config surface and changes which durable memory artifacts enter recall context, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape or backend scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95739 or a successor after fixing merge semantics, index identity, docs, and explicit builtin-only scope while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause exclusion work until builtin indexing, QMD collections, watcher behavior, stale-index cleanup, docs, and diagnostics share one accepted path-scope model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and focus this issue on clearer path-drift, broad-extraPaths, and benchmark-contamination guidance plus status warnings.

recommendation.title: Narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95739 or a successor after fixing merge semantics, index identity, docs, and explicit builtin-only scope while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history on QMD/memorySearch path semantics and docs/config shape among the likely owners.
